project.name: Electric Stability Control (ESC) — Concept Phase Safety Case

confirmation_reviews.reviewer: Dr. Sarah Williams (HW Safety Engineer, Different Team)

open_items.description: SW safety requirements verification coverage data pending integration test completion
HW FMEDA DC% refinement for one minor failure mode pending final diagnostic implementation

executive_summary_text: The Electronic Stability Control (ESC) ECU has been developed in accordance with ISO 26262:2018 to ASIL D. The HARA identifies five safety goals (SG-001 through SG-005) addressing loss of yaw rate control, sensor signal corruption, and actuator command failures. All safety goals are allocated to functional safety requirements (FSRs) in the FSC, with decomposition employed for two of the five goals per DFA coupling analysis. The FSC allocates FSRs to the Electronic Control Unit node with resulting ASIL C (post-decomposition). Technical Safety Concept refines these to six HW-TSRs and eight SW-TSRs, with mechanisms including dual-core lockstep, E2E protection, and watchdog timers. Hardware FMEDA demonstrates compliance with SPFM >= 99%, LFM >= 90%, and PMHF < 10 FIT. Software verification includes statement and branch coverage >= 95% for ASIL D code, plus MC/DC for critical decision logic. All confirmation reviews completed with required independence. The item is acceptably safe for integration into the Mid-Size Sedan 2027 program.
